# Jadpo

> An experimental, statically typed programming language for web backends written mainly by LLMs and reviewed by people. The compiler and runtime are written in Rust, with interpreted development and compiled native and WebAssembly deployables.

This is a reading index, not the language specification or a guarantee of automatic retrieval. Follow the linked area pages for rules, current decisions, amendments and implementation status. Decided does not mean built. Do not infer the language from the README or a small example alone.

The public project home is https://github.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo. Links below track main; use a single checkout or replace main with one commit SHA throughout when a consistent snapshot matters. A URL tool may require every relevant link explicitly. GitHub and the assistant's tools determine access; this file changes no crawler permissions.

## Start here

- [Primer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/primer.md): Read this first before writing an app: layout, syntax, the constructs nearly every app uses, what is built and where to look next; 3,000 to 5,000 tokens, every example compiled.
- [Learn Jadpo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/learn/README.md): A todo app with sign-in, built a page at a time from an empty folder to a deployed server, for a newcomer; every page's project compiled and tested.
- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/agent-skill/SKILL.md): The skill for a coding agent that writes Jadpo apps: read the primer, find pages, run `jadpo check --json` and `jadpo test --json`, and report a Jadpo bug through the user.
- [Project README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/README.md): Purpose, a compiler error example, status and how to build from source.
- [Language map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/README.md): Task-based reading paths and all 21 specification areas.
- [Examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/README.md): Every complete teaching project, with comments and tests, and the closest one for each feature.
- [Vision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/vision.md): Why Jadpo exists and how responsibility is divided.
- [Roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/roadmap.md): The only implementation tracker; separates outstanding work from completion.
- [Compiler and runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/compiler-runtime.md): The graph, interpreter, compiled targets and verification architecture.

## Language specification

Each area page holds what an app author reads; its design notes, the reasons and decisions, are in docs/language/notes/. Each compiler error has its own page, `docs/errors/<rule.id>.md` (for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/errors/failure.kind_required.md), and the error's `help:` line prints its address on the site, `https://jadpo.dev/docs/errors/<rule.id>`. Start with areas 1–4. For a data-backed authenticated API, add 5–9 and 13. For integrations and background work, add 10–12, starting with area 11's "How packages, connections, capabilities and services fit together". For AI features, read 21 and its linked rules. For design review, read 9 and 15–18, keeping their planned features distinct from implemented checks.

- [1. Project layout and modules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/01-project-layout-and-modules.md): Domains, paths, visibility, imports and naming.
- [2. Values and types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/02-values-and-types.md): Named types, validation, refinements, objects, enums and collections.
- [3. Logic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/03-logic.md): Functions, actions, expressions, control flow and effects.
- [4. Failures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/04-failures.md): Declared failures, handling, propagation and runtime faults.
- [5. Data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/05-data.md): Entities, relationships, storage and migrations.
- [6. Reads and writes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/06-reads-and-writes.md): Queries, pagination, aggregates, transactions and concurrency.
- [7. HTTP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/07-http.md): Routes, contracts, API records and OpenAPI.
- [8. Identity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/08-identity.md): Principals, sessions, tokens, keys, magic links and passkeys.
- [9. Policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/09-policy.md): Ownership, grants, roles, tenancy and field access.
- [10. Configuration and time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/10-configuration-and-time.md): Settings, secrets, connections, time and translations.
- [11. Integrations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/11-integrations.md): Provider packages, connections, capabilities, webhooks and recordings.
- [How packages, connections, capabilities and services fit together](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/11-integrations.md#how-packages-connections-capabilities-and-services-fit-together): What a package, provider, connection, driver, capability, built-in service and service run by Jadpo each are, where each runs in development, tests, native and Workers deployables, and what is built; Docker or Podman is used only for a service run by Jadpo (`runs:`), which is not built yet. Read this before areas 10, 11 and 16.
- [12. Jobs and events](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/12-jobs-and-events.md): Events, outbox delivery, subscribers, schedules and batches.
- [13. Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/13-testing.md): Test kinds, fixtures, databases, fakes and controlled clocks.
- [14. Tooling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/14-tooling.md): CLI commands and implementation status, formatting, editor support and deployables.
- [15. Personal data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/15-personal-data.md): Export, erasure, retention and privacy reporting; largely planned.
- [16. Built-in services](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/16-built-in-services.md): Email, files, rate limits, search, audit and telemetry; status varies.
- [17. Debugging and review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/17-debugging-and-review.md): Source-level evidence, request explanations and behaviour review; planned.
- [18. Records and manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/18-records-and-manifest.md): Committed contracts, generated manifests and planned approvals.
- [19. Standard library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/19-standard-library.md): Vocabulary types and operations, money, units, text and formats.
- [20. Geospatial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/20-geospatial.md): Geometry, geodesic operations, PostGIS and map layers.
- [21. AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/21-ai.md): Prompts, typed model calls, streaming, embeddings, budgets and personal-data flow.

## Complete application examples

Every teaching project in examples/, in reading order. Read each README, then the source files and tests it lists.

- [01-first-project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/01-first-project/README.md): the project root, a domain, named types, `use` lines, a function, actions and tests.
- [02-named-types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/02-named-types/README.md): every built-in representation, the rules a type can add, refinements, literals and conversions.
- [03-objects-and-enums](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/03-objects-and-enums/README.md): objects, inputs and outputs, field types, absent values, enums and tagged unions, and types built from other types.
- [04-lists-and-loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/04-lists-and-loops/README.md): lists and sets, `for`, `var mut`, and the `collection` operations with inline functions.
- [05-logic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/05-logic/README.md): operators, `if` chains, every form of `match`, division with rounding, and recursion.
- [06-failures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/06-failures/README.md): declaring failures, `fails`, `reject`, `attempt`, checks that can fail, a condition that proves one can't, and handling failures with `match`.
- [07-testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/07-testing/README.md): test kinds, fixtures, and asserting failures.
- [08-domains-and-sharing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/08-domains-and-sharing/README.md): several domains, `public`, `shared/`, libraries, `use <domain>`, a public fixture, and a scenario in `tests/`.
- [09-bakery-orders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/09-bakery-orders/README.md): a fuller project that puts all of it together.
- [10-library-loans](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/10-library-loans/README.md): stored records: entities, references, unique rules and indexes, the migrations that keep the database in step with them, the queries that read them, and the writes that change them: updates, patches, deletes, conflicts and a counter.
- [11-cake-shop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/11-cake-shop/README.md): HTTP and sign-in: route groups, inputs from the query string, the body and a header, statuses, APIs and their records, deadlines and idempotent writes, browser sessions, API tokens and service keys, the caller passed to actions, simple grants, and route tests that sign in.
- [12-recipe-book](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/12-recipe-book/README.md): policy for many customers in one application: tenancy, membership roles, actions listed with who may run them, field restrictions, a role across the whole application and the permissions report.
- [13-lettings-office](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/13-lettings-office/README.md): settings: `config.jadpo`, a setting's types and defaults, the connections' addresses, constants, test values, and the keys a `crypto` call takes without code reading them: sealing, passwords, a shared secret, a private key and another service's tokens.
- [14-studio-timetable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/14-studio-timetable/README.md): time: zones, times a rule repeats on, opening hours, ranges of time, a day's, week's, month's and year's bounds, calendar arithmetic and periods, the night the clocks change, and times shown to people.
- [15-parcel-tracker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/15-parcel-tracker/README.md): translations: messages, a language file per locale, plural forms, enums with wording, a message two domains share, the reader's language and direction, Jadpo's own text and a language still in progress.
- [16-market-hall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/16-market-hall/README.md): money: amounts in minor units, currencies fixed by a type, rounding, prices and deals, percentages, sharing to the penny, rates, cards and amounts shown to people.
- [17-ebike-hire](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/17-ebike-hire/README.md): physical quantities: types with bounds in units, kinds that combine, units only at the edges, every kind's units by name, exact decimal maths, and quantities a person typed.
- [18-village-newsletter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/18-village-newsletter/README.md): text and the web: text operations, Markdown and rich text made safe, text in each language, links, colours, images, networks, tokens, digests and encodings.
- [19-book-club](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/19-book-club/README.md): lists, sets and maps, numbers, randomness, codes in other code systems, versions, a rule across a type's fields and declining a standard type.
- [20-fell-race](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/20-fell-race/README.md): geography in code: points, lines and polygons, distances, bearings, lengths and areas on the ellipsoid, inside, across and near, boxes and circles, polygons valid when built, WKT and GeoJSON layers.
- [21-veg-box-rounds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/21-veg-box-rounds/README.md): stored places: PostGIS columns, queries nearest first, in a box, a circle or an area, the indexes they need, a map layer from a query, counts and sums by month, and a backfill worked out from each row.
- [22-plant-helpline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/22-plant-helpline/README.md): stored vectors, the nearest query and its tuned index, distance in code, and prompts: checked prompt files, rendering, a shared prompt and a conversation.
- [23-repair-cafe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/23-repair-cafe/README.md): events: declaring and emitting them, the outbox, subscribers and their retries, events that cause events, the event record, an action that only emits, and routes that answer 202 or wait for the follow-on work with `settle:`.
- [24-seed-library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/24-seed-library/README.md): batches: work over many items a page at a time, an action per item, problems, the summary at the end, `key:`, a run's status and cancelling it, and a standard operation in a query's condition.
- [25-allotment-rents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/25-allotment-rents/README.md): schedules, and background work in an application with tenants: a schedule reaching every tenant, a subscriber and a batch reaching one.
- [26-delivery-desk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/26-delivery-desk/README.md): packages: an installed library package locked by its digest and used through its name, and the app's own integration with a provider's API in the package format, called through a connection; webhooks, a package's subscribers, events and poll, a recipe, recordings, a mail package and a queue filling capabilities, two versions side by side with a package's words, an OpenAPI import mapped to standard types, and several changing calls kept as steps.
- [27-guest-house](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/27-guest-house/README.md): email and signing in by email: an email as a type, its HTML and text templates checked against its fields, its subject worded like a message, the shared layout and a shared partial, sending by emitting after commit, the SMTP connection, tests that read what they sent, magic-link sign-in with routes and a sign-in email of the app's own, a link's token and a code, Jadpo's own words in another language, sign-in events, and passkeys, recovered through a magic link.
- [28-lost-property](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/28-lost-property/README.md): AI: a model package and its connection, budgets, embeddings one at a time and many at once, a search by meaning, typed answers from a model, personal data sent to it, a stream sent to a route, the fake every test answers through, and recorded answers.
- [29-lending-desk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/29-lending-desk/README.md): customers and staff in one app: customers signing in by magic link, staff with Google through a sign-in provider, two staff roles held across the whole app, a listed staff query beside a customer catalogue, staff taken on by a seed, and a due-date reminder schedule over a batch, each with its route or schedule test.

## When Jadpo is wrong

If the compiler crashes, rejects code the docs say is valid, accepts code the docs say it refuses, or a page is wrong: check the error's page and the docs first, then cut it down to the smallest project that still shows it. Ask your user before filing anything, because a public issue is published under their name. Give them the drafted report, or a prefilled link to the [bug form](https://github.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=). Include no secrets, settings values or app code beyond that project. After a crash, `~/.cache/jadpo/crashes/` holds a file for the report; your user reads it before it is attached. Never post on your own. A suspected security hole goes to the private route in [SECURITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/SECURITY.md), never a public issue.

## Contributing to the compiler

- [Contributor guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Build prerequisites, verification and contribution workflow.
- [Repository instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/AGENTS.md): Working rules for changes to this compiler repository.
- [Documentation index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/README.md): Architecture, decisions and design context.
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/benchmarks/README.md): The golden todo, its TypeScript twin and contract cases, and the harnesses that measure Jadpo against TypeScript.
- [CLI design language](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/cli-design-language.md): How everything `jadpo` prints, and every generated page, looks and behaves.
